correctness.rationale: The retained claim is the ordered distinct-prime two-block limit. Independently rescaling each input gives the event uv≥B. PNT on fixed intervals [sX,tX) yields mass (t−s)/(B−1) after division by the block count; the Cartesian product gives the limiting rectangle probabilities without assuming anything about primes in short intervals. The hyperbola has zero limiting area, and the diagonal exclusion costs at most reciprocal block size in equal blocks and nothing otherwise. The section length B−B/u integrates to the announced constant. The elementary finite criterion is true but is now background, not a separate contribution. The rounded constants agree with direct evaluation.
residual_risks: No density over semiprimes ordered by product is established; the packaged finite counts are corroborative only.

value.rationale: After excluding the already covered finite digit observation as a standalone result, the asymptotic answers a natural prevalence question: with the input lengths prescribed, how often does a squarefree semiprime occupy the larger of the two possible product lengths? It gives a precise base-dependent benchmark for this conditional sample, rather than counts in an arbitrary finite slice or an assertion of a global density. It combines the finite criterion with a genuinely different distributional calculation, even though the proof is short.
residual_risks: No convergence rate or comparison with the global natural density is claimed.
